statement: The supplied sources genuinely contain no derivation of the concept Lie algebra; the heading 'Derivations' in the source refers to algebraic derivations (linear maps satisfying the Leibniz rule $D(xy) = D(x)y + xD(y)$), not a mathematical derivation of Lie algebra. A Lie algebra is an algebraic object defined as a vector space $\mathfrak{g}$ over a field $F$ equipped with a Lie bracket operation $[\cdot, \cdot]: \mathfrak{g} \times \mathfrak{g} \to \mathfrak{g}$ satisfying the Lie algebra axioms (including $[X, X] = 0$ and the Jacobi identity). For matrix Lie algebras, the bracket is the commutator $[X, Y] = XY - YX$.

symbols.meaning: Lie algebra (a vector space over a field $F$ equipped with a Lie bracket)
adjoint mapping (inner derivation) defined by \mathrm{ad}_x(y) = [x, y]
Lie algebra of derivations of \mathfrak{g} over field $F$
matrix commutator bracket XY - YX in a matrix Lie algebra

properties.property: For two Lie algebras $\mathfrak{g}$ and $\mathfrak{g}'$, the product Lie algebra is $\mathfrak{g} \times \mathfrak{g}'$ with bracket $[(x, x'), (y, y')] = ([x, y], [x', y'])$, where copies of $\mathfrak{g}$ and $\mathfrak{g}'$ commute: $[(x, 0), (0, x')] = 0$.
properties.why: Defines the product in the category of Lie algebras componentwise.

properties.property: Every one-dimensional linear subspace of a Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ is an abelian Lie subalgebra.
properties.why: The axioms imply $[X, X] = 0$, so any one-dimensional subspace has a trivial Lie bracket.

properties.property: For any algebra $A$, the space $\mathrm{Der}_F(A)$ of derivations forms a Lie algebra under the commutator bracket $[D_1, D_2] := D_1 D_2 - D_2 D_1$.
properties.why: The commutator of two linear maps satisfying the Leibniz rule is itself a derivation.

properties.property: The adjoint mapping $\mathrm{ad}_x(y) := [x, y]$ is an inner derivation of $\mathfrak{g}$, providing a Lie algebra homomorphism $\mathrm{ad}: \mathfrak{g} \to \mathrm{Der}_F(\mathfrak{g})$.
properties.why: Satisfies the derivation Leibniz rule on brackets as a consequence of the Jacobi identity.

properties.property: The inner derivations $\mathrm{Inn}_F(\mathfrak{g})$ form an ideal in $\mathrm{Der}_F(\mathfrak{g})$, and outer derivations are defined by the quotient $\mathrm{Out}_F(\mathfrak{g}) = \mathrm{Der}_F(\mathfrak{g}) / \mathrm{Inn}_F(\mathfrak{g})$.
properties.why: Formed as the quotient Lie algebra of all derivations modulo the ideal of inner derivations.

properties.property: For a matrix Lie group $G \subset \mathrm{GL}(n, \mathbb{R})$, the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ is the space of tangent vectors $c'(0)$ to smooth curves $c: \mathbb{R} \to G$ with $c(0) = I$, equipped with commutator bracket $[X, Y] = XY - YX$.
properties.why: Constructs the Lie algebra as the tangent space to a matrix Lie group at the identity.

assumptions.assumption: The underlying space $\mathfrak{g}$ is a vector space over a field $F$ equipped with a bracket operation satisfying the Lie algebra axioms.
assumptions.breaks_when: The scalar structure fails linearity over a field or the bracket fails the required algebraic relations (e.g. $[X, X] = 0$ or Jacobi identity).

assumptions.assumption: For matrix Lie groups, curves $c: \mathbb{R} \to G$ passing through $I$ are smooth.
assumptions.breaks_when: Curves fail to be differentiable, preventing the definition of tangent vectors $X = c'(0)$.

failure_modes.mode: Subspace fails to be a Lie subalgebra
failure_modes.signature: The bracket of two elements in a linear subspace produces an element outside the subspace.
failure_modes.cause: The linear subspace is not closed under the Lie bracket operation.

failure_modes.mode: Subalgebra fails to be an ideal
failure_modes.signature: There exist $x \in \mathfrak{g}$ and $y \in \mathfrak{h}$ such that $[x, y] \notin \mathfrak{h}$.
failure_modes.cause: Closure under internal brackets (subalgebra) does not imply stability under brackets with elements of the ambient algebra.

failure_modes.signature: There exists a derivation $D \in \mathrm{Der}_F(\mathfrak{g})$ that cannot be written as $\mathrm{ad}_x$ for any $x \in \mathfrak{g}$.
failure_modes.cause: The Lie algebra is not semisimple over characteristic zero (e.g., an abelian Lie algebra where $\mathrm{Out}_F(V) \cong \mathfrak{gl}(V)$).
